marble.name: The Heart & Blood
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Understand that the heart is a muscle that pumps blood around the body through tubes called blood vessels, and that we can feel our heartbeat by placing a hand on our chest or fingers on our wrist
marble.prompt: Can you find their own pulse on their wrist or neck, and explain that it’s their heart pumping blood?

cluster.summary: Your child is discovering how their amazing body works — learning about the heart, lungs, brain, skeleton, and five senses, plus understanding what their body needs to stay healthy and strong.

misconceptions: Thinking the heart is shaped like the ❤ symbol, rather than a fist-sized muscle.
Believing the heart is on the far left edge of the chest rather than roughly centre-left.
Thinking blood is blue inside the body and turns red only in air — blood is always red.
Believing the heart only 'beats' with emotions (love/fright), not that it pumps blood every second of life.
Thinking blood just sits still in the body or only appears when you are cut, rather than constantly circulating.
representations: A fist held up to show the heart's real size and location (centre-left of chest)
A soft squeeze-ball as a stand-in pump the child works with their hand
Pulse points (wrist, neck) the child presses to feel the beat
A simple body outline with tubes (vessels) branching to hands, feet and head
A rest-vs-running heartbeat comparison (slow thump → fast thump)
authoredAnswer: The heart is beating and blood is moving all the time, even sitting still — it beats faster when you run but never stops. Both the finger and the toe bleed because blood travels through tubes (blood vessels) to every part of the body, so blood is everywhere, not only in one spot and not only when you exercise.

wrongAnswers.wrong: It only beats when you run — when you sit still it stops.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Says the heart rests or stops when sitting still.
wrongAnswers.fix: Feel the pulse while sitting still to prove it beats now; explain it speeds up with exercise but never stops.

wrongAnswers.wrong: Only the finger would bleed, because that's where the blood is.
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Expects only the finger to bleed; treats blood as localised.
wrongAnswers.fix: Use the two-cuts evidence: both bleed because vessels carry blood everywhere; trace vessels reaching hands and feet.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Describes the heart's job as holding feelings, not pumping blood.
wrongAnswers.fix: Distinguish the everyday 'heart' symbol from the organ; the real heart is a muscle that pumps blood.
